manifest.system: You are a helpful assistant. Explain clearly and concisely.
manifest.warmup:
Our town library is reviewing its reservation service. Members search the catalogue, choose a title, and join a waiting list when every copy is on loan. Staff contact the next member when a returned copy becomes available. Reserved books remain at the collection desk for three working days. Members can update their contact details through an online account. The service sends email reminders before a reservation expires. Staff help members who cannot use the website and record telephone reservations in the same queue. Each title has its own waiting list ordered by reservation time. A member can cancel a reservation without losing a place on another list. The library wants shorter waiting times and fewer uncollected books. Its budget allows small changes to messages and staff procedures, but no additional building or large software purchase. Staff will review outcomes weekly using reservation counts, cancellations, and collection delays. 
Summarize this.

candidates.A: A coastal research team is studying damage to coral reefs. They record water temperature, rainfall, salinity, and the number of fish at several sites. Volunteers photograph the same reef sections every month. Some sites are close to busy harbours, while others are protected from boats and fishing. The team has a limited budget and wants reliable comparisons across locations. Explain how they should organize the observations and avoid misleading conclusions.
candidates.B: A city transport team is reviewing bus reliability. Drivers report delays at crowded junctions and passengers report missed connections. The team has arrival records from stops, traffic counts, and anonymous passenger surveys. Some routes serve schools, others serve hospitals, and several share a congested bridge. The city can adjust schedules and stop locations but cannot purchase new buses this year. Explain how the team should choose improvements and measure their effects.
